queue_items.claim: The row's self-declared primary warrant, an a-fortiori dependency running across the seam, is byte-false because the particle it rests on is verse-internal, leaving the cluster on a root the row itself concedes is non-exclusive and whose word-bound recurrence binds a non-adjacent verse instead.
queue_items.grounds: The row's device_notes state that the pairing's force rests on the a-fortiori dependency between the two verses and not on root-exclusivity, and strongest_rejected_alternative grounds that dependency on 'the particle opening 19:7'. Spliced byte-tier, Prov.19.7 reads כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי רָ֨שׁ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לא לוֹ הֵֽמָּה: it opens on כָּ֥ל, a quantifier, and the a-fortiori pair אַ֤ף כִּ֣י stands at words 5 and 6 with the etnahta on word 9, מִמֶּ֑נּוּ - so that particle governs the relation between Prov.19.7's own cola, not the relation across the seam, and no particle opens the verse at all. What remains is the friend-root, and word-bound skeleton sweeps show it does not bind this pair: the form at Prov.19.6, הָ֝רֵ֗עַ, is word-bound in 2 of 915 verses (Prov.17.17, Prov.19.6), and the form at Prov.19.7, מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ, is word-bound in 3 of 915 verses (Prov.12.26, Prov.19.4, Prov.19.7); the two sets do not intersect, and the word-bound recurrence actually links Prov.19.7 to the NON-adjacent Prov.19.4, which the row itself discloses while still carrying the cluster. OW-3 both-sides on both seams: at the leading seam the preceding row's closing verse Prov.19.5 reads עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט and the row's opening verse Prov.19.6 reads רַ֭בִּים יְחַלּ֣וּ פְנֵֽי נָדִ֑יב וְכָל הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן, sharing no word-bound skeleton token; at the trailing seam the row's closing verse Prov.19.7 and the following row's opening verse Prov.19.8, קֹֽנֶה לֵּ֭ב אֹהֵ֣ב נַפְשׁ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֥ר תְּ֝בוּנָ֗ה לִמְצֹא טֽוֹב, likewise share none - so both outer edges are clean and the only live boundary is the seam INSIDE the row, which carries no word-bound shared token either. C2's ruled default is single_proverb with proverb_cluster only on byte-grounded cohesion named in the rationale; the cohesion named here is a discourse dependency the bytes place inside one verse, on top of a root the row itself declines to call exclusive.
queue_items.proposed_change: Retire the two-verse cluster and atomize to the collection default: one row Prov.19.6-Prov.19.6 and one row Prov.19.7-Prov.19.7, both unit_type single_proverb, parent_collection unchanged at C2 Prov.10.1-Prov.22.16, confidence re-opened as a dependent field of the driver swap along with observed_substrate_signals and strongest_rejected_alternative. The Prov.19.7 row then carries the a-fortiori structure as its OWN internal device (אַ֤ף כִּ֣י at words 5-6, etnahta on מִמֶּ֑נּוּ at word 9) plus its scribal disclosures (the staged inventory records one ketiv/qere note and one paseq seg at Prov.19.7, single-witness, the paseq layer count-only), and discloses as texture the word-bound friend-token it shares with the non-adjacent Prov.19.4 (3 of 915 verses). The Prov.19.6 row carries its own friend-token (2 of 915 verses word-bound) and the gift-giver theme it shares with Prov.19.4 as texture, never as cluster grounds. This is a candidate proposal for owner triage and applies nothing to any shipped corpus.

queue_items.claim: The statement that Prov.19.7 opens its second colon with the friend-form is byte-false under the verse's own accentuation and under a tricolon reading alike.
queue_items.grounds: Prov.19.7 is fourteen whitespace tokens - twelve reading tokens plus the inline ketiv/qere pair at words 12-13 - with the etnahta on word 9, מִמֶּ֑נּוּ. The accentual second half is therefore מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לא לוֹ הֵֽמָּה, which opens on מְרַדֵּ֖ף, while the friend-form מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ stands at word 7 inside the first half; on the alternative tricolon reading the second colon opens on אַ֤ף כִּ֣י, not on the friend-form either. So the claim that the verse opens its second colon with that form is byte-false on both readings. The mark disclosures in the same sentence do check out against the staged inventory - one ketiv/qere note and one paseq seg are recorded at Prov.19.7, the row cites both with the single-witness qualifier, and it makes only a verse-level paseq claim, which is all the count-only inventory can source. This repair applies if the span is left standing after triage of the higher finding on this row.
queue_items.proposed_change: Replace the clause that the verse opens its second colon with the friend-form by an accurate placement - מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ stands at word 7, inside the first half-verse, the etnahta being on מִמֶּ֑נּוּ at word 9 - and replace 'the particle opening 19:7' in strongest_rejected_alternative with 'the a-fortiori pair אַ֤ף כִּ֣י at words 5-6 of Prov.19.7', together with the disclosure that it governs that verse's own two cola rather than the seam.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Both verses carry the same friend-root רע in the mercenary-friendship theme: 19:6 closes וְכָל הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן “everyone is a friend to a man who gives gifts” (web:Prov.19.6), and 19:7 opens its second colon with מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ “his friends avoid him” (web:Prov.19.7) — the same root turned from the flatterer's calculus (v.6) to the poor man's abandonment by that same class of "friend" (v.7), a deliberate two-verse elaboration of one social observation rather than two unrelated maxims. 19:7 also carries a ketiv/qere pair at its closing word (לא/לוֹ); a paseq mark sits in the same verse. (oshb:Prov.19.6; oshb:Prov.19.7)
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 19:6 and 19:7 as independent is rejected because 19:7's opening colon ("all the relatives of the poor shun him") completes the a-fortiori logic 19:6 sets up — if everyone chases the gift-giver, how much more do even kin flee the poor; the particle opening 19:7 grammatically depends on the claim just made in 19:6.
observed_substrate_signals: shared root at the same "friend" sense in both cola
K/Q and paseq co-occurring at 19.7
shipped_row.device_notes: Two-verse elaboration of mercenary friendship; the weaker of this part's clusters, resting more on discourse-logic (dependency) than on an exact repeated lexeme. The friend-root also recurs at 19:4 (oshb:Prov.19.4), non-adjacent; the pairing's force rests on the a-fortiori dependency between 19:6 and 19:7, not on root-exclusivity.

queue_items.claim: observed_substrate_signals asserts an exact repetition at the same line-final slot, which the row's own rationale correctly denies and the bytes disprove.
queue_items.grounds: Spliced byte-tier, Prov.19.13 reads הַוֺּ֣ת לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וְדֶ֥לֶף טֹ֝רֵ֗ד מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה - eight words with the etnahta on word 4, so the second colon is words 5-8 and the wife-noun אִשָּֽׁה is both colon-final and verse-final. Prov.19.14 reads בַּ֣יִת וָ֭הוֹן נַחֲלַ֣ת אָב֑וֹת וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת - seven words with the etnahta on word 4, so the second colon is words 5-7 and the wife-noun אִשָּׁ֥ה is colon-medial at word 6, exactly as boundary_rationale states. The observed_substrate_signals entry claiming an exact repeated noun 'at the same line-final slot' therefore contradicts the row's own rationale on the slot, and overstates the repetition on tier: the two forms differ at byte tier and, because accent_stripped retains meteg, at accent_stripped tier too, being identical only at consonantal-skeleton tier. The warrant and the high confidence survive the correction on independent bytes - a word-bound skeleton sweep of the wife-noun returns 9 of 915 verses (Prov.6.26, Prov.6.32, Prov.7.10, Prov.11.22, Prov.18.22, Prov.19.13, Prov.19.14, Prov.30.20, Prov.31.30) and Prov.19.13 with Prov.19.14 is the ONLY adjacent pair among them, while both first cola carry the father-root (לְ֭אָבִיו at Prov.19.13 word 2, אָב֑וֹת at Prov.19.14 word 4), which the rationale argues but oss never records. OW-3 both-sides: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.19.12, נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר זַ֣עַף מֶ֑לֶךְ וּכְטַ֖ל עַל עֵ֣שֶׂב רְצוֹנֽוֹ, shares no word-bound skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.19.13, and the row's closing verse Prov.19.14 shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.19.15, עַ֭צְלָה תַּפִּ֣יל תַּרְדֵּמָ֑ה וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ רְמִיָּ֣ה תִרְעָֽב - both edges hold.
queue_items.proposed_change: Rewrite the first observed_substrate_signals entry to match the rationale and name its tier: the wife-noun recurs across the pair at consonantal-skeleton tier - verse-final at Prov.19.13 word 8, colon-medial at Prov.19.14 word 6 - and Prov.19.13 with Prov.19.14 is the only adjacent pair among the 9 of 915 verses carrying it word-bound; add a second entry for the father-root shared by the two first cola (לְ֭אָבִיו at Prov.19.13 word 2, אָב֑וֹת at Prov.19.14 word 4), which is argued in the rationale but missing from the evidence field.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The exact same noun אִשָּֽׁה/אִשָּׁ֥ה "wife/woman" runs across both verses' second colon in antithesis: 19:13's מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה "a wife's quarrels" closes the verse's second colon (colon-final, verse-final), alongside "a foolish son" in the first colon; 19:14's אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת "a prudent wife" instead sits colon-medial in the second colon, occupying the predicate-complement slot immediately after the fronted "from Yahweh" phrase and before the closing "prudent" adjective, alongside "house and riches" as merely human inheritance in the first colon. Both verses pair a father/inheritance first colon with a wife-named second colon, the same two-part frame run twice with opposite content. (oshb:Prov.19.13; oshb:Prov.19.14)
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the verses as unrelated maxims is rejected because the deliberate repetition of the same wife-noun — verse-final in 19:13, colon-medial in 19:14 — sets up a contrast (quarrelsome wife/dripping vs. prudent wife/Yahweh's gift) that only works read as a pair; taken alone, 19:14's implicit contrast with the preceding verse's wife-image is not recoverable.

queue_items.claim: The rationale's etnahta placement claim is byte-false on either reading of its parenthetical, and device_notes carries the byte-true version, so the row contradicts itself.
queue_items.grounds: Spliced byte-tier, Prov.20.5 reads מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים עֵצָ֣ה בְלֶב אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה יִדְלֶֽנָּה - eight words with the etnahta on word 5, which IS the bare man-noun אִ֑ישׁ - and Prov.20.6 reads רָב אָדָ֗ם יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא - nine words with the etnahta on word 5, חַסְדּ֑וֹ, the bare man-noun standing at word 4, אִ֣ישׁ. The rationale says the bare man-noun 'stands ahead of the verse's own etnahta in both (word 5 of 8 in 20:5, word 5 of 9 in 20:6)'. Read as the noun's own position, 'word 5 of 9' is false at Prov.20.6, where the noun is word 4; read as the etnahta's position, the digits are right but 'stands ahead of the verse's own etnahta in both' is false at Prov.20.5, where the noun carries the etnahta itself. device_notes states the byte-true asymmetry in terms, so the two fields disagree with each other. Everything else in this row re-swept exactly and it is the best-evidenced cluster in this slice: the same-verse bare-plus-waw-prefixed doubling, word-bound at consonantal-skeleton tier, returns 2 of 915 verses and both hits are Prov.20.5 and Prov.20.6; the bare form word-bound returns 53 of 915; the contiguous-substring sweep returns 87 of 915. OW-3 both-sides: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.20.4, מֵ֭חֹרֶף עָצֵ֣ל לֹא יַחֲרֹ֑שׁ ישאל וְשָׁאַ֖ל בַּקָּצִ֣יר וָאָֽיִן, shares no word-bound skeleton token with the row's opening verse Prov.20.5, and the row's closing verse Prov.20.6 shares none with the following row's opening verse Prov.20.7, מִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֣וֹ צַדִּ֑יק אַשְׁרֵ֖י בָנָ֣יו אַחֲרָֽיו - so the row's rejection of an extension to either neighbour holds on bytes, and the waw-prefixed second instance does open the second colon in construct with an abstract quality noun in both verses (וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה and וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים).
queue_items.proposed_change: Re-cut the rationale's parenthetical to the reading device_notes already carries: a bare man-noun stands in the first half of both verses - carrying the etnahta itself at Prov.20.5 word 5 of 8, and standing one word ahead of the etnahta-bearing חַסְדּ֑וֹ at Prov.20.6 word 4 of 9. Leave observed_substrate_signals unchanged: its etnahta entry is already byte-true, and its two sweep digits re-verify exactly.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: מַ֣יִם עֲ֭מֻקִּים עֵצָ֣ה בְלֶב אִ֑ישׁ וְאִ֖ישׁ תְּבוּנָ֣ה יִדְלֶֽנָּה (oshb:Prov.20.5) and רָב אָדָ֗ם יִ֭קְרָא אִ֣ישׁ חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְאִ֥ישׁ אֱ֝מוּנִ֗ים מִ֣י יִמְצָֽא (oshb:Prov.20.6) run one shared construction: a bare man-noun, איש, stands ahead of the verse's own etnahta in both (word 5 of 8 in 20:5, word 5 of 9 in 20:6), and a waw-prefixed second instance of that noun, ואיש, answers it just past the caesura in both, opening the second colon in construct with an abstract quality noun — תבונה, "understanding," in 20:5 and אמונים, "faithfulness," in 20:6 — before both verses close on that second colon's own predicate, ידלנה in 20:5 and מי ימצא in 20:6. A word-bound sweep of this same-verse bare-plus-waw-prefixed doubling (whitespace-token equality against the consonantal skeleton) returns 2 of 915 verses book-wide, and both hits are the two verses of this span. The bare noun by itself, word-bound, is far more common (53 of 915 verses), and a contiguous-consonantal-substring sweep of the same bare form is wider still (87 of 915 verses); the paired, colon-symmetric doubling sets this pair apart from that wider background.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 20:5 and 20:6 as two unrelated proverbs was rejected: the bare-plus-waw doubling that opens each verse's second colon is not the ordinary recurrence of a common noun but a paired, colon-symmetric construction, and a word-bound sweep of that exact doubling returns 2 of 915 verses book-wide, both of them this pair, so the two verses read as one deliberately constructed unit; extending the span to include Prov.20.4 or Prov.20.7 was also rejected, since neither neighboring verse shares a skeleton content token with either member of the pair.
observed_substrate_signals: same-verse bare-plus-waw doubling of the man-noun (word-bound, whitespace-token equality): 2 of 915 verses book-wide, both members of this pair
etnahta lands on word 5 in both verses (word 5 of 8 in Prov.20.5; word 5 of 9 in Prov.20.6)
the waw-prefixed second instance opens the second colon and stands in construct with an abstract quality noun in both verses
shipped_row.device_notes: The bare instance of the man-noun sits in a different slot in the two verses: it carries the etnahta itself in Prov.20.5, but stands one word ahead of the etnahta-bearing word in Prov.20.6. The two verses also run distinct images — deep water drawn out for hidden counsel in Prov.20.5, a claim of loyalty set against a rhetorical question about scarce faithfulness in Prov.20.6 — so the pairing runs a synthetic image in Prov.20.5 against a synthetic claim answered by an antithetic question in Prov.20.6, two different couplet textures joined by the shared bare-plus-waw construction.

queue_items.claim: device_notes calls both verbs third-person jussive wishes, but the first is indicative in the row's own reading and in the second witness's rendering.
queue_items.grounds: The row's boundary_rationale calls Prov.23.24 the general maxim about a righteous child's parent, and the second witness renders it “The father of the righteous has great joy. Whoever fathers a wise child delights in him.” (web:Prov.23.24) - indicative, not a wish; only Prov.23.25 is rendered as a wish, “Let your father and your mother be glad! Let her who bore you rejoice!” (web:Prov.23.25). At byte tier the qere forms are יָ֭גִיל and יִשְׂמַח at Prov.23.24 against יִֽשְׂמַח at Prov.23.25, and the staged extract carries no morphology layer, so mood has to be argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses rather than asserted for both verses at once. The conclusion the claim was recruited to support still holds independently: neither verse carries a governing second-person imperative or vetitive, so the span does stand outside the operative admonition_unit category of its collection, and the deviation disclosure is properly present in device_notes as the collection amendment requires.
queue_items.proposed_change: Split the mood claim: state that Prov.23.25 opens on a third-person wish, יִֽשְׂמַח, rendered “Let your father and your mother be glad!” at web:Prov.23.25, while Prov.23.24 is indicative on both witnesses' readings; and rest the deviation disclosure on the shared absence of a governing second-person imperative or vetitive rather than on a jussive label applied to both verses.

queue_items.claim: The row rejects only the atomization rival and never tests the extension rival, though a byte-visible parental frame brackets its opening edge two verses back.
queue_items.grounds: OW-3 both-sides on the leading seam: the preceding row's closing verse Prov.23.23 reads אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל תִּמְכֹּ֑ר חָכְמָ֖ה וּמוּסָ֣ר וּבִינָֽה and the row's opening verse Prov.23.24 reads גול גִּ֣יל יגול יָ֭גִיל אֲבִ֣י צַדִּ֑יק יולד וְיוֹלֵ֥ד חָ֝כָ֗ם וישמח יִשְׂמַח בּֽוֹ; the only object crossing that seam is the wisdom root, חָכְמָ֖ה at Prov.23.23 word 5 against חָ֝כָ֗ם at Prov.23.24 word 9, and a word-bound skeleton sweep of the latter returns 26 of 915 verses - a common token, correctly demoted to a textural echo by the preceding row, whose digit re-swept exactly - so that seam holds and the row's span is defensible. The trailing seam is clean too: the row's closing verse Prov.23.25, יִֽשְׂמַח אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ, shares no word-bound skeleton token with the following row's opening verse Prov.23.26, תְּנָֽה בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י וְ֝עֵינֶ֗יךָ דְּרָכַ֥י תרצנה תִּצֹּֽרְנָה. What is untested is the extension rival. A second-person parental pair brackets the row's opening edge two verses back: a contiguous-skeleton sweep of the father-form returns 5 of 915 verses (Prov.1.8, Prov.6.20, Prov.23.22, Prov.23.25, Prov.27.10) and of the mother-form 4 of 915 (Prov.1.8, Prov.6.20, Prov.23.22, Prov.23.25), so Prov.23.22, שְׁמַ֣ע לְ֭אָבִיךָ זֶ֣ה יְלָדֶ֑ךָ וְאַל תָּ֝ב֗וּז כִּֽי זָקְנָ֥ה אִמֶּֽךָ, and the row's own closing verse are two of only four verses in the book carrying that pair, while the begetting root runs across Prov.23.22, Prov.23.24 and Prov.23.25 under mater-lectionis variation (יְלָדֶ֑ךָ, then וְיוֹלֵ֥ד, then יֽוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ). That is a live larger-unit reading of Prov.23.22-Prov.23.25 which neither this row nor its neighbours name, and strongest_rejected_alternative tests only the atomization rival. I record it as an untested rival for owner triage and do NOT propose the respan: the row's own seam catchword is the tighter object - the qere verb at Prov.23.24 word 11 and the opening verb of Prov.23.25 are the same word-bound skeleton token, whose sweep returns 11 of 915 verses with both of them among the hits - and the intervening Prov.23.23 carries its own governing imperative-plus-vetitive frame. The row's ketiv/qere arithmetic also re-checks exactly: the staged inventory records 4 ketiv/qere notes at Prov.23.24, matching the four pairs the row names, cited single-witness.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Verse 24 carries four ketiv/qere pairs in one line -- גול/גִּ֣יל, יגול/יָ֭גִיל, יולד/וְיוֹלֵ֥ד, וישמח/יִשְׂמַח (oshb:Prov.23.24, ketiv/qere, single-witness) -- and its qere verb יִשְׂמַח recurs at the head of verse 25, יִֽשְׂמַח אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ (oshb:Prov.23.25, 'let your father and mother be glad'), the shared root binding the general maxim about a righteous child's parent to its applied wish for this son's own parents.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading verse 24 alone as the row and verse 25 as a separate single_proverb was considered, given the topical shift from general maxim to direct wish, but was set aside because the repeated root binds the two into one developing statement.
observed_substrate_signals: four ketiv/qere pairs sit in one verse (Prov.23.24, single-witness)
the qere verb at 23:24 recurs as the opening verb of 23:25
shipped_row.device_notes: Synthetic pair: general maxim, then its personalized application, joined by a repeated root; the K/Q density leaves the exact wording of verse 24 less certain than the boundary decision itself. Both יָ֭גִיל (oshb:Prov.23.24, ketiv/qere, single-witness) and יִֽשְׂמַח (oshb:Prov.23.25) are third-person jussive wishes about the parents' own joy, not a governing second-person imperative or vetitive, so the span stands outside C3's operative admonition_unit category by its own grammar.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: אֱמֶ֣ת קְ֭נֵה וְאַל תִּמְכֹּ֑ר (oshb:Prov.23.23, 'buy the truth, and do not sell it') is a governing second-person imperative-plus-vetitive command filling the whole verse -- קְ֭נֵה an imperative, וְאַל תִּמְכֹּ֑ר a vetitive -- lacking a following motive clause. No exact wordform repeats at either seam; the honor-your-parents command before it (oshb:Prov.23.22) shares no root, while the father's-joy couplet after it does share a cognate: the wisdom root named here in חָכְמָ֖ה (oshb:Prov.23.23) recurs in nominal form as חָ֝כָ֗ם (oshb:Prov.23.24; word-bound exact token, 26/915 verses book-wide) -- a textural echo, not a shared boundary word.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the verse as a single_proverb on the strength of its lacking a motive clause was set aside: the mood test C3 applies to its admonition_unit default fires on the governing imperative-plus-vetitive frame regardless of a following motive clause, and admonition_unit is the value that fits wherever that frame governs the span.
observed_substrate_signals: a governing imperative-plus-vetitive command fills the whole verse (Prov.23.23)
no exact wordform repeats at either seam; a cognate wisdom root recurs at 23:24 (word-bound exact token, 26/915 book-wide)
prev_row.device_notes: A self-contained commercial-metaphor command (buy/do not sell) rather than a bare maxim; the imperative-plus-vetitive frame governs the whole span even without a motive clause.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A third vocative opens the unit, תְּנָֽה בְנִ֣י לִבְּךָ֣ לִ֑י (oshb:Prov.23.26, 'give me your heart, my son'), carrying its own ketiv/qere note, תרצנה/תִּצֹּֽרְנָה (oshb:Prov.23.26, ketiv/qere, single-witness); verse 27 supplies the motive with כִּֽי (oshb:Prov.23.27) and the deep-pit/narrow-well image for the unfaithful wife, and verse 28 continues that image, closing a three-verse vocative-plus-motive unit that reads as the collection's compressed version of the strange-woman warnings developed at length in chapters 1-9.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Stopping the unit at verse 26 alone was rejected because the motive clause of verse 27 supplies the rationale the vocative command needs, and verse 28 continues rather than restarts that image.
observed_substrate_signals: a vocative and imperative open the unit, with a ketiv/qere note (Prov.23.26, single-witness)
a motive clause with the deep-pit image follows (Prov.23.27)

queue_items.class: E-23 cluster warrant rests on an English-visible image field
queue_items.claim: The row's load-bearing binder, stated as the shared building-image vocabulary of house, established and rooms, is not a lexical sharing at all, because Prov.24.3 and Prov.24.4 share zero skeleton content tokens, and the rival single-proverb atomization is set aside on that same image ground.
queue_items.grounds: Re-derived at skeleton tier, the token sets of 24:3 and 24:4 intersect in the empty set; the three items the row names are בָּ֑יִת and יִתְכּוֹנָֽן, both inside 24:3, and חֲדָרִ֣ים in 24:4 -- three different lexemes standing in one image field that is fully visible in translation, not a repeated token or root, so the warrant is tier-4 topic affinity and cannot carry a cluster, and the confidence of high rests on it. The byte object that does bind the pair goes unnamed: the instrumental bet plus wisdom-triad series בְּ֭חָכְמָה and וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה in 24:3 continued by וּ֭בְדַעַת opening 24:4, a three-member colon-initial series whose members are the same triad that co-occurs at Prov.2.6 and that runs across a verse boundary in the same order at Prov.3.19 and Prov.3.20 (בְּחָכְמָ֥ה, בִּתְבוּנָֽה, בְּ֭דַעְתּוֹ) alongside כּוֹנֵ֥ן, the same root that 24:3 carries in יִתְכּוֹנָֽן. All quoted runs are byte tier, spliced from the staged verse map and re-collated at their cited refs; the zero-overlap result is skeleton tier. The span itself is not challenged by this finding: it survives on the unnamed series, so the repair is a warrant replacement.
queue_items.proposed_change: Replace the binder clause in boundary_rationale and the matching signal in observed_substrate_signals: name the instrumental bet plus wisdom-triad series (בְּ֭חָכְמָה and וּ֝בִתְבוּנָ֗ה at 24:3, וּ֭בְדַעַת opening 24:4) as the cohesion object at skeleton tier, state that 24:3 and 24:4 share zero skeleton content tokens so the pair is bound by the series rather than by a repeated lexeme, and drop house-established-rooms to a device_notes image note; the replacement passes the test that killed the original because its members are byte objects at named refs rather than glosses. strongest_rejected_alternative re-opens with it and must reject the atomization on the series rather than on the completed figure. Confidence may stay at high only on the replaced warrant. Proposal only; nothing is applied.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: בְּ֭חָכְמָה יִבָּ֣נֶה בָּ֑יִת (oshb:Prov.24.3, 'through wisdom a house is built') opens a declarative image rather than an imperative; verse 4 continues the same house image with חֲדָרִ֣ים (oshb:Prov.24.4, 'rooms... filled'), the shared building-image vocabulary (house, established, rooms) binding the pair as one developing figure rather than two unrelated maxims.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading verses 3 and 4 as two separate single_proverb rows was set aside because verse 4's rooms-filled-with-treasure image completes rather than restarts the house-building figure verse 3 opens.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The chapter opens with אַל תְּ֭קַנֵּא בְּאַנְשֵׁ֣י רָעָ֑ה (oshb:Prov.24.1, 'do not envy evil men'), a fresh topic after the wine poem closes at 23:35, carrying its own ketiv/qere note, תתאו/תִּ֝תְאָ֗יו (oshb:Prov.24.1, ketiv/qere, single-witness); verse 2 supplies the motive with כִּי (oshb:Prov.24.2, 'for their hearts plot violence'). The same verb root recurs at Prov.24.19, a non-adjacent bracketing of the chapter's opening and closing prohibitions rather than a link within this pair.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending the unit to include verse 3's wisdom-builds-a-house maxim was rejected because verse 3 shares no root with the envy prohibition and opens a distinct declarative topic.

next_row.boundary_rationale: גֶּֽבֶר חָכָ֥ם בַּע֑וֹז (oshb:Prov.24.5, 'a wise man is in strength') opens a strength/power image distinct from the house-building figure just closed at 24:4; verse 6 opens with the causal particle כִּ֣י (oshb:Prov.24.6, 'for'), its clause בְ֭תַחְבֻּלוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה לְּךָ֣ מִלְחָמָ֑ה ('by strategies you wage war') explaining how the wise man's strength in v.5 is exercised -- a motive-clause warrant, not a repeated-vocabulary one.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 24:5-6 as a continuation of the 24:3-4 house-building cluster was rejected since no building-vocabulary token repeats past verse 4, and the strength/war image opens its own figure at verse 5.
